scope: Independent primary-form/static assembly and adversarial stage review. This is not finished-source, animation, integration, exact historical-vehicle identification or general production-ready approval.
method: Inspected complete current canonical sheet and complementary views; then inspected lit diagnostic sheet and all 17 Bradley 256px frames individually.
Rehashed all nine canonical views and current GLB. Rehashed all68 lit diagnostic frames, both model GLBs and comparison sheet.
Decoded actual GLB source-space vertices and indexed triangles. Compared all newly replaced part point clouds with typed r3 recipe at1e-6m tolerance.
Checked bidirectional triangle-edge/surface intersections for hull vs both tracks, side armor vs its track and terminal wheels; inspected support geometry and prior unchanged r2 repairs.
Compared stage shape and semantic allocation with previously inspected Army/period sources and presentation-neutral grounded-tactical-miniature-visual@1.0.0 profile.

nose.observation: Full-width nose restored; longitudinal shoulder closes the accidental triangular forebody notches while preserving upper profile.

currentGeometry.staticSupportStatus: Hatch, ramp and launcher support repairs remain; ring connects turret body to hull, mantlet connects retained gun. No regression observed.
currentGeometry.retainedWheelBeltStatus: R2 wheel/belt geometry retained; all road and terminal wheel polygons remain within/tangent to inner belt cavity. End wheels no longer protrude beneath outer belt.
currentGeometry.limitation: These checks establish listed static relationships, not continuous motion/suspension/turret sweeps, interior fidelity or universal mesh nonintersection.

closure.limits: Exact stations and hidden ring remain disclosed reconstruction; no fine equipment/variant fidelity claim.

recognitionAt256.context: Native256px canvases at shared world span12.780914965m; Bradley occupies substantially less than full canvas, so this is conservative common-world-scale evidence. Reviewer knew identity; not a blinded classification trial.
cues: Tall slab-sided troop hull with forward glacis, compared with Abrams' lower longer main-battle-tank body.
Short cannon and smaller polygonal turret rather than Abrams' long gun and large angular turret.
Six visible road wheels and raised terminal track runs in side views.
Physical-left turret launcher block, two crew roof discs and forward sight allocation in top/oblique/map views.
Rear ramp/access-door and paired port cues in rear views.

viewCoverage.assessment: Weakest specific-variant views because shared worldscale yields small silhouette; coherent tall hull, offset upper masses and rear access face remain visible. Fine A2-specific fittings not claimed.
Six-wheel stance, rising track ends, tall troop compartment and short-gun turret remain legible.
Turret/mantlet, side launcher, glacis, rear deck and ramp allocation read coherently without a privileged hero angle.
Lit presentation separates roof elements and launcher; front/rear direction and compact IFV form remain stable across map azimuths.

recognitionAt256.limits: No direct nearest-neighbor lineup or blinded M2A2-versus-M2A1 test was performed. Exact variant detail belongs to supported primary/secondary refinement; evidence supports this declared coarse blockout decision.

projectStyle.comparison: Bradley r3 alongside approved Abrams v1.0 at common world scale and lighting.
compatibleAtBlockout: Restrained desert service color, dark running gear, planar hull/armor and legible mass hierarchy.
Bradley remains smaller/shorter and visibly an IFV, preserving scale/role contrast rather than copying Abrams proportions.
No noisy texture, excessive microdetail or invented markings introduced.
deferred: Bradley has deliberately lower detail density than finished Abrams; refine functional secondary forms, curved barrel/launcher details and restrained edges after blockout decision.
Final material vocabulary and edge treatment require later exact evidence; this stage does not certify finished style parity.

adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: No unresolved blockout-core objection after complementary256px views show tall troop hull, six-wheel stance, short gun and left launcher; exact variant/finished recognition remains a later requirement.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Nose shoulder cuts or merged turret/launcher masses could undermine identity.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: R3 closes nose cuts; lit plan/oblique evidence distinguishes turret and launcher. No new primary silhouette regression found.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Hidden skirts could intersect moving bands even if rendered silhouette looks correct.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: Actual GLB clearance and surface-crossing checks close the identified static clashes. Motion qualification explicitly excluded.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Passing producer checks might conceal stale diagnostics or unsupported source equivalence.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: Current checkpoint/GLB/view hashes and all diagnostic source pins verified. Listed structural checks are current. Remaining formal evaluator/human gates are not represented as completed.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Simplification might remove functional primary masses rather than merely omit detail.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: Required coarse turret/launcher/crew-roof/running-gear masses are present; deferred detail is appropriate to blockout.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Uniform extrusion or accidental discontinuities could conflict with grounded miniature form language.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: Tapered polygonal turret and continuous nose resolve identified defects; refined edge treatment remains deferred.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Painted top faces could merge and lose functional hierarchy.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: Supplemental lit packet reveals required masses without source mutation; canonical flat-view limitation remains disclosed.

adversarialCoreChallenges.strongestChallenge: Hero framing or different scales could hide weaknesses relative to baseline.
adversarialCoreChallenges.stageDisposition: All native/map azimuths use same worldscale alongside Abrams and remain unclipped. Presentation-neutral profile does not impose an unrelated atlas contract.
